extraFacts.fact: JIS hose fittings of the B 8363 family seat on a 30° cone (60° included), while SAE J514 JIC fittings seat on a 37° flare; the two are not interchangeable even where the threads look alike, so identify the seat before ordering.
extraFacts.source: JIS B 8363 as cited on the Indus JIS listings, compared with SAE J514 (37° flare)

extraFacts.fact: The SAE dash number is the size in sixteenths of an inch: -04 is 1/4 in, -06 is 3/8 in, -08 is 1/2 in, -10 is 5/8 in, -12 is 3/4 in, -16 is 1 in, -20 is 1-1/4 in, -24 is 1-1/2 in, -32 is 2 in, which is how the hose dash column of the Indus JIS listings is written.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 / J514 dash-size convention, matched against the hose dash and hose inch columns of the Indus JIS size tables

extraFacts.fact: SAE four-bolt split flange ports are Code 61 and Code 62 (SAE J518 / ISO 6162); the JIS flange head used on Japanese excavators and presses differs in bolt pattern and face and does not interchange with them.
extraFacts.source: SAE J518 / ISO 6162, and the Indus JIS Flange Hose Fitting listing

faqs.q: What is the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting used for?
faqs.a: The 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting is a 45° elbow hydraulic hose fitting for Japanese-pattern equipment, with a flange face. The 45° elbow of the JIS flange family.

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-JP-FLANGE-45-12 on the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting?
faqs.a: The last two digits of an Indus JIS flange part number give the hose dash: in IH-JP-FLANGE-45-12, 12 is the 3/4" hose. All three sizes share the same 5/8" thread entry, so the dash is the only size choice on this listing.

faqs.q: What sizes does the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting come in?
faqs.a: The 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting is listed for hose from 1/2" (dash -08) to 3/4" (dash -12), and every row carries the same 5/8" thread entry. Choose the row by the hose dash size and quote the part number from the size table.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size of 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting?
faqs.a: Choose the hose dash size first; the port thread entry on this listing is the same for every size, so confirm that your flange head matches the JIS pattern before ordering. The [guide to fittings on a used Japanese machine](/blog/fittings-on-a-used-japanese-machine) explains how to identify the seat and thread from the machine.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting?
faqs.a: No pressure rating is published for the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting itself, because the hose grade and bore set the rating of the finished assembly. Tell us the hose grade, bore and working pressure on your enquiry and we confirm the figure in writing before supply.

faqs.q: What is the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting made of, and how is it finished?
faqs.a: The 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting is made of carbon steel, finished Zinc-plated, Cr3+ passivated, RoHS-compliant. 316 stainless steel is available on request for corrosive or marine service, so say so on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which standard does the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting follow?
faqs.a: The listing for the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting cites JIS B2291 for the flange head, and it is not interchangeable with an SAE Code 61 or 62 flange, because the bolt pattern and the face differ. No third-party certificate is attached, so tell us any test or material document the order needs.

faqs.q: What does the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting connect to?
faqs.a: The 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting bolts to a JIS flange port on the machine and crimps onto hose of the matching dash size; it does not fit an SAE Code 61 or 62 port. Tell us the hose grade and we specify the ferrule and crimp; see also the [SAE flange fittings](/c/sae-flange-fittings) if the port is SAE.

faqs.q: How do I fit and tighten the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting?
faqs.a: Fit the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting to a clean, undamaged flange face, tighten the bolts evenly, and keep it square to the port so the flange face seals. Check the face for scoring before refitting; the [inspecting fittings on arrival](/blog/inspecting-fittings-on-arrival) guide lists what to look for.

faqs.q: How does the 45° JIS Flange Hose Fitting differ from the JIS Flange Hose Fitting?
faqs.a: The two sit in the same Japanese-fitting family and the names differ by “45°” being added in this name. The [JIS Flange Hose Fitting](/p/jis-flange-hose-fitting) has its own size table, so compare the rows to see which one lists the hose and thread you need.
